tagline: From the pottery village up to the old cliff town.
intro: Indian Road 565 starts at Santa Clara Pueblo, close by Española, and heads west across Santa Clara land toward the Jemez Mountains. It is the only state scenic byway in New Mexico that lies entirely on a pueblo.

At the end of it stands Puye, a town cut into a cliff of soft volcanic tuff, where up to 1,500 people once hunted and farmed. Drought sent them down toward the Rio Grande, and the people of Santa Clara, some ten miles east, count themselves their descendants. In 2000 the Cerro Grande Fire burned through Santa Clara Canyon. The site has since reopened.

moments.title: Santa Clara Pueblo
moments.text: A Tewa village on the Rio Grande whose potters are known for polished black and red wares with deep engravings, where knife-wing and eagle feather designs are common.

moments.title: Puye Cliff Dwellings
moments.text: Paths and some twelve stairways and ladders climb a 200-foot cliff past two levels of carved rooms, about 740 of them, to a pueblo on the mesa top.

practical: Visitors to the cliff dwellings check in at the Puye Cliffs Welcome Center, and tours can be scheduled; Santa Clara Pueblo has current information.
